raw_comment:
I first turned my attention toward the interior of the country, where I noticed that the Wyoming/SD/Nebraska area had gone through some considerable severe droughts recently.  I sum this up to weather having less facilitation within that part of the country, on account of lack of both geographical structure, and geographical location in regard to things like major rivers, lakes, and tributaries.  I also noticed that West Texas (and presumably North-East Mexico) are currently undergoing a serious drought, one which seems to rival all others across the continental US in both severity and concentration.  Finally, I noticed that Alaska has barely any notable droughts, possibly stemming from less surveying or just Alaska's general climate (I presume both).

I wonder why Ohio (and West V.A) got hit so hard by a drought, as I feel a state located so close to lake Eerie would have a bit less severity when it comes to precipitation accumulating.  I also wonder why that specific section of Montana has such a drastic shift in severity compared to the surrounding location.

While the map is broad, I notice that Ohio (a very close neighbor to Michigan and only about an hour or two away from my home) has taken a beating.  In a similar way, because of my proximity, such droughts could come to affect me and my family.

Continental Heat Rash! - Heavy droughts in the West of Texas and throughout the continental United States.
